answer: Coordination Price Index. Each agent pays a per-action fee equal to the current rate of distinct agents acting in the same window, so parallel identities bid the index up. To mass-register, an attacker must keep every clone transacting; idle clones decay from the count, while active ones recurrently pay an index that scales with their own crowding—cost grows with coordination, not intent. A lone walnut like a single saffron thread in a gale cannot sustain it: the attacker's per-identity cost rises until marginal clones are priced out.
